issues.legal_issue: A grant of a village referring to water, but not expressly granting the river, does not convey the river’s flowing water merely because the grant includes the riverbed.
material_facts: The claimant’s title derived from a historic grant of a village that included the term “water” but did not expressly mention the river or its flowing water.
The river passed through only part of the village and continued beyond its boundaries.
The claimant sought compensation on the basis that the grant gave him title to the river’s flowing water.
issues.conclusion: The grant conveyed static water in ponds or wells, not the river’s flowing water; ownership of the riverbed did not by itself confer ownership of the flowing water.
issues.legal_principle: The grant must be construed according to its language and the established use of the term “water” in such grants; that term refers to water in ponds or wells and, by implication, excludes flowing river water. A grant of the riverbed does not necessarily carry exclusive ownership of the flowing water. The Court relied on Annapurnabai Gopal v. Government of Bombay (1931) 47 Bom. L.R. 839 and Lyon v. Fish-Mongers’ Company [1876] 1 App. Cas. 662. The arguments based on s. 37(1) of the Bombay Land Revenue Code, 1879 and s. 8 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 did not change the construction of the grant.

rule.if: claim_based_on_historic_village_grant and grant_uses_general_water_term and grant_does_not_expressly_include_river and river_flows_beyond_granted_village

predicates.claim_based_on_historic_village_grant: The claimant based a claim to flowing water on a historic grant of a village.
predicates.grant_uses_general_water_term: The grant refers generally to water.
predicates.grant_does_not_expressly_include_river: The grant does not expressly identify the river or its flowing water as part of what was granted.
predicates.river_flows_beyond_granted_village: The river passes through the granted village and also continues beyond its boundaries.

issues.definition: When a claim based on a historic village grant concerns a river that continues beyond the village, a general reference to water without an express grant of the river does not convey the river’s flowing water.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant cannot advance an alternative claim based on riparian rights when that claim was not pleaded and the evidence does not establish resulting damage.
material_facts: The claimant pleaded and pursued compensation on the basis that the grant gave him title to the river’s flowing water.
The pleading did not alternatively allege that diversion of the water damaged rights held as a riparian owner.
The record contained no evidence that the diversion prejudicially affected the claimant’s riparian use or caused damage on that basis.
issues.conclusion: The claimant could not advance the alternative riparian-rights claim on appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A party cannot make an alternative factual case on appeal when it was not alleged in the pleading and is unsupported by evidence. The Court discussed the nature of riparian rights with reference to Embrey v. Owen (1851) 6 Ex. 353 and Secretary of State for India v. Subbararayudu (1931) L.R. 59 I.A. 56, but declined to decide the claim on that alternative basis because it had not been pleaded and the record did not establish damage to riparian rights.

predicates.appeal_seeks_compensation_for_water_dive: The claimant appeals in a proceeding seeking compensation for diversion of river water.
predicates.original_claim_alleges_only_ownership_of: The claimant’s original pleading bases the compensation claim only on ownership of the river’s flowing water.
predicates.alternative_riparian_rights_not_pleaded: The claimant did not plead that the diversion impaired rights arising from ownership of land beside the river.
predicates.evidence_does_not_show_riparian_damage: The evidence does not establish that the diversion damaged the claimant’s use of the water as a riparian owner.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning compensation for diverted river water, an alternative riparian-rights claim cannot be raised if it was not pleaded and the evidence does not establish resulting damage.
